user: For this same charge, what evidence of non-delivery should I keep?
answer:
For a goods-not-received dispute, the knowledge base says to keep:

- **Order confirmation** for the purchase
- **Delivery record**, such as a tracking number, carrier status, or a "not delivered" notice
- **Correspondence with the merchant** about the order, including any replies or attempts to resolve it

The Verta process also says the customer may be asked for supporting evidence. If that evidence isn't supplied within 7 calendar days of the request, the case is declined. So keep these records together and be ready to send them quickly.

I haven't opened a dispute yet. Eligibility for this charge has already passed, but I'll need your confirmation before I file it. If you'd like, I can also look into the earlier charge to the same merchant. A possible duplicate would fall under a different reason code (duplicate_charge), which needs its own eligibility check and different evidence.

fragments.text:
Dispute handling process
## Evidence requirements
The customer may be asked for supporting evidence: an order confirmation, a
delivery record, correspondence with the merchant. Failure to supply requested
evidence within 7 calendar days results in the case being declined.

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Glossary
## Provisional credit
A temporary refund applied while a dispute is reviewed; reversed if the dispute
is declined.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |
